content: Granules used for mosquito larval control can be applied either from aircraft or with a motorized knapsack sprayer that has been adapted for granular application. Manual granule applicators specifically designed for mosquito control are generally not widely available. However, several types of manually carried granule applicators, originally marketed for agricultural use, can be repurposed for mosquito larval control. Insecticides formulated as granules vary in size, composition, and recommended application rates, necessitating calibration of the equipment with the specific insecticide product before field use. General Requirements for Granule Applicator Equipment: 1. Materials: All materials used in the construction of granule applicators must resist corrosion and chemical degradation, ensuring durability and proper functioning during normal use. 2. Design: The applicator must be designed to prevent granules from being trapped on its outer surfaces, regardless of the hopper's fill level. All fittings should be free of sharp edges or projections to avoid injury to operators. 3. Weight: The maximum weight of the equipment, when filled to its recommended capacity, must comply with national health and safety regulations. In the absence of such regulations, the maximum weight should not exceed 25 kg for knapsack equipment or 20 kg for hand-carried equipment. 4. Hopper: The hopper must have a secure lid to prevent spillage and dust escape. It should not be mounted in front of the operator and must not cause granules to break or create dust. The hopper should be designed for complete emptying and, if the opening is less than 90 mm wide, a funnel or closed transfer system should be used for filling. 5. Flow Control: A device must be included to regulate the release of granules, either as a single dose or for spreading over a wider area. 6. Straps: They must pass drop tests without failure. 7. Markings: The equipment must clearly display the manufacturer’s name, contact details, machine type, date of manufacture, serial number, and key component positions. 8. User Manual: A clear, illustrated manual must accompany the equipment, detailing operation, calibration, safety precautions, maintenance, and spare parts. The manual should be available in the local language of the country where the equipment is marketed. Specific Types of Granule Applicators: 1. Manually Carried (Shoulder-Mounted) Applicators: These consist of a shoulder-slung bag made of durable material and a delivery tube. The bag should have a zippered opening for easy filling and a tapered metal discharge tube with a flow adjustment device. The fully loaded unit should not exceed 12 kg in weight. Granules are applied by swinging the discharge tube side-to-side to distribute them evenly over a 7-meter swath. 2. Hand-Carried Granule Applicators: These consist of a tube to hold granules, which fall by gravity to an outlet controlled by a hand-operated mechanism. The tube must have a wide opening for filling, a secure lid to prevent spillage, and an adjustable release mechanism. The unit’s weight, when fully loaded, should not exceed 5 kg. 3. Knapsack Granule Applicators: These include a container mounted on a frame with straps for comfortable back carrying. The container must have a large opening (at least 12 cm in diameter) for quick filling and a tight lid to prevent dust escape. A delivery tube with a dose regulator and on/off valve is required. 4. Motorized Knapsack Mist Blowers Adapted for Granules: These units feature a container above an engine-driven fan that projects granules over a swath of at least 5 meters. The engine must have an easy-start mechanism, a fuel tank allowing at least one hour of operation, and controls visible to the operator. The equipment must include padded straps and a backrest for operator comfort, with vibration dampening during use. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): International standards for protective clothing are available, and guidelines for PPE use are under development by FAO/WHO. Durability and Testing: For example: Tanks must withstand repeated pressurization cycles without failure. Straps must endure repeated drop tests without damage. Calibration and Maintenance: Maintenance procedures, including cleaning and part replacement, should be followed as outlined in the user manual to maintain equipment performance and safety.
